pageCache.pageTitle: Benenden Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Adventurous Together
Welcome to Benenden Church of England Primary School
Alison BrookHeadteacher
Welcome to Benenden Church of England Primary School! Our Vision is to be a learning community that enables people to live life in all its fullness in a changing world. (John 10:10) In order to do this, we strive to ensure that our school is happy, hard working and community focused.
Our community thrives outdoors in nearly all weather conditions, engaging in play, communication, and learning within the diverse outdoor spaces on our site. We don’t even have ‘wet play’! Bordering sheep fields, our students have extensive access to a wide range of outdoor learning experiences. This includes our new outdoor learning hub, forest school, access to the wellbeing garden, and extra-curricular activities such as campfires, sleepovers and residential trips.
Through these opportunities, children can truly experience ‘life in all its fullness’. They develop a love for learning and a drive to challenge themselves, building the resilience to persevere and the teamwork skills to achieve their aspirations in a safe and supportive environment.
Do have a look at our website to find out more, or I would be very pleased to show you around our incredible building. However, the best way to discover what Benenden CEP is all about, is for the children to explain!

Wellbeing
We are delighted to have been awarded our Wellbeing Accreditation for Schools in recognition of the importance we place on putting wellbeing at the centre of everything we do.
Benenden Final Verification Report
If you have any comments or feedback regarding our strategy, please email Aimee Davis directly on senco@1010federation.org
Mental Health and Wellbeing Policy 2026-2028
Parent Wellbeing Workshop
Thank you to all of our parents who attended the Parent Workshop on Wellbeing which was organised based on feedback from our parent survey. For any parents who were unable to come, please see the PowerPoint detailing the Wellbeing provision in school for our pupils. Thank you also for your comments during this session which were very gladly received and which will help to inform our provision going forwards.
Parent Wellbeing Workshop
At our next planned workshop, we shall be joined by our Spurgeons Family Support worker - Clare Craggs. Further information to follow.
Provision in School
Should a child need a little more support at any time, the school provides many support mechanisms which can help. Our Pyramid of Wellbeing Provision shows you the layers of support available to your child, dependent on their level of need:
Universal means the support available to all children, all of the time.
Early support means a slightly higher level of support, using readily available resources in school.
Targeted help means a higher level of support and possible referrals for some more specialist support and/or family support.
Specialist support means the highest level of support we can offer in school and includes support from external agencies with more specialist knowledge and experience such as our Play Therapist or Counsellor.
You can find more information about interventions below.
Within the school day, children are provided with a variety of opportunities to monitor and express how they are feeling. This includes feelings charts in the classroom that are monitored by staff - providing the children with opportunities to talk. Each class is following the SCARF PSHE Scheme www.coramlifeeducation.org.uk where the children learn more about how the mind works and strategies linked to emotional wellbeing, such as breathing techniques. The school uses a ‘Trackit light’ system, which primarily rewards positive behaviour throughout the day, but also enables the teacher and SLT to monitor whether there are any behaviours that may indicate that the child is emotionally struggling, and to provide further support.
In addition to this, we have a school Therapy Dog called Fudge. Fudge adores working with the children and has a special talent for spotting who might need some cuddles. He is on a timetable across all the classes in KS1, KS2 and attends Forest School.
Should a child need a little more support at any point, the school offers:
A named trusted adult to touch base and check on the child
Access to the Hedgehog room at lunchtimes to discuss problems or to have access to a safe, calm space.
A ‘drawing & talking’ intervention using trained TA’s. https://drawingandtalking.com/
Play therapy with our trained Play Therapist lotusplaytherapy.wixsite.com/website

Special Educational Needs
Removing Barriers to Learning: Quality First Teaching and Support for All
Inclusive Teaching and Learning
We are committed to inclusion. We endeavour to make every effort to achieve maximum inclusion of all pupils whilst meeting their individual needs as learners.
What do we mean by Special Educational Needs?
Children have Special Educational Needs if they have a learning difficulty that calls for special educational provision to be made for them. They may have:
They may have difficulty with one or more of the following:
We know that children learn and develop in different ways so we use different teaching styles, resources and plan different levels of work, along with many other approaches. This is called Quality First Teaching.
How do we identify children who need extra support?
We aim to keep the time between identifying where support is needed and responding with the right provision to a minimum. Home and pre-school visits help with early identification and enable us to plan for future provision. As well as this we liaise with parents, health professionals and early years settings (nurseries) to build a sound evidence base.
Once in school, your child will be assessed in a number of different ways, including class observation. From these assessments your child’s teacher will be able to see what they are good at, where they need help and how best you can help at home.
What happens if your child is identified as needing support?
If your child needs support in one of the four areas mentioned, the class teacher, together with the SENCO will decide the type and level of support, which may change throughout their time at school. We will always keep you informed and part of the process.
What does the SENCO do?
SENCO = Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator
If your child needs support, the SENCO will:
What could the support look like?
The support could be within class, as part of a small group or one to one help. The class teacher and SENCO will best assess which type and level of support needed.
For your child this action will be enough to help them to overcome any difficulties and help them make good progress.
Sometimes, additional advice from outside specialists is needed, which could include advice from specialist teachers, educational psychologists, speech and language therapists or physiotherapists. In this case we work alongside parents and professionals to carry out further assessments and form an individual provision plan.

As well as this we liaise with parents, health professionals and early years settings (nurseries) to build a sound evidence base.

If your child needs support in one of the four areas mentioned, the class teacher, together with the SENCO will decide the type and level of support, which may change throughout their time at school. We will always keep you informed and part of the process.
What is an Individual Provision Plan?
This is essentially what your child’s class teacher and the SENCO plan to do to help your child. It will include short term targets, extra support detail (i.e. how often the support is being given) and when the school will next look at progress.
These plans are reviewed throughout the year and then discussed with parents at Parent’s Evening. Your child would also be discussed at regular Pupil Progress meetings throughout the school year.
If you have a concern about your child’s learning then your child’s class teacher is the first person to talk to as they plan for ways to give support in class, whether that support be one to one or in a group.
You can also contact our SENCO Nicola Bryant n.bryant@benenden-cep.kent.sch.uk

Sports Premium
Sports Funding
PE & Sport Grant
The Department for Education has awarded a PE & Sports grant again to schools this year. Schools with at least 17 primary age pupils will receive £16,000 plus £10 per eligible pupil for the current year.
Purpose of funding
Schools must spend the additional funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this. Hiring specialist PE teachers or qualified sports coaches to work with primary teachers when teaching PE.
Benenden Church of England Primary School employ a specialist PE teacher one day a week to teach PE throughout the school. The teacher, Maria Mileham also runs an after school club and trains teams and squads for competitions. Other sports clubs are run after school by other members of staff.
On top of the Kent School Games festivals and competitions, Mrs Mileham also enters children for competitons at Independent and secondary schools. Where appropriate she has also sent children to county trials in football, cross country and Sportshall Athletics.
In addition, we pay to be part of the Tunbridge Wells School Sports partnership exit package; this gives us support with schemes of work and assessment as well as access to staff training.
The staff at our school have been delighted with the support that the partnership has given us so far. Teachers have stated that they feel more secure about delivering PE lessons because they use strategies that they have observed Mrs Mileham and TWSSP staff using. They feel more confident about developing the children's skills in their own lessons, using advice from Mrs Mileham each week.
We are delighted that once again we have been awarded The School Games Gold Kitemark 2024-25

Year 6 Woodpeckers
Meet the Teaching Team
Welcome to Woodpeckers Class!
Welcome to what I'm sure will be a memorable final year of primary school at Benenden. The year 6 team are so excited to see you all and begin our final year of learning.
In our final year at Benenden, we will not only cover the curriculum learning but we also aim to ensure that our children are 'secondary ready'. We hope that our Year 6 children will become more independent, resilient and reflective as learners and have a lot of fun along the way too! Highlights of the year include looking after a Reception Class buddy, a week long residential trip and taking a leading part in the summer play. In addition to our in class learning, Forest School is an integral part of school life and Woodpecker class will enjoy several sessions in the school forest as well as numerous outdoor learning opportunities.
This year, several trips/ learning opportunities, both away from and within school have been organised to supplement our learning. We aim to ensure all children leaving us, demonstrate and continue with our school values: Curiosity, Compassion, Courage and Commitment.

Meet the Governors
Oliver Miller Chair of Governors
Oliver Miller
Working within the hospitality and facilities management sector, I bring a wealth, strategy and service expertise to the Governing Board. With two children at Benenden, and with a keen interest in cultivating supportive and engaging school communities, I work closely with the school leadership team and other governors to set and develop sustainable and long-term strategic plans.
Being a keen sports enthusiast, I also am a strong advocate for well-being and mental health, ensuring that the schools have the right support and guidance to meaningfully support our students.
Committed to the best outcomes for all pupils, I have monitoring responsibility for finance, leadership management and health and saftey. Originally joining as a parent governor in 2020, and becoming Vice-Chair, I am now Chair of Governors.
Simon Cullen Co-opted Governor
Simon Cullen
I joined the governing body of the school in February 2018 and am a parent of two children, one who is still at Benenden Primary School. I am Assistant Head and Head of Sixth Form at Benenden Girls' School and I hope to be able to bring some of my experience of teaching and middle management to help take The Federation forward in meeting all of its goals.
Reverend Rachel Robertson Foundation Governor
Reverend Rachel Robertson
I've been a Foundation Governor since January 2021 when I became Vicar of St Mary's, Goudhurst with Christ Church, Kilndown. My role is to help ensure the Christian ethos of the school is secure and lived out on a daily basis. I spend time in Goudhurst & KIlndown school every week, particularly for Collective Worship on Wednesdays, and love encouraging the staff and pupils. I have three teenagers, and live in Goudhurst.
Alison Brook
I am Head of School (Benenden) responsible for Behaviour and Attitudes and Personal Development across the Federation. I am a strong advocate for outdoor learning to be offered within the curriculum as it adds so much to the engagement of the learning, as well as encouraging development of resilience, problem solving and communication skills-to name but a few! When not at school I enjoy running, scouting and spending time with my family. I lead worship at church, and play in a barn dance band.
Ryan Laker
Aimee Day
I joined the Federation In January 2022 as Assistant Head and SENCO at Goudhurst and Head of Personal Development and Wellbeing across the Federation. I was appointed Fedeartion Senco in September 2024. Having been in education for the past 16 years, I have worked in a range of larger schools across both Bromley and Kent, but not any as small as Goudhurst and Benenden. It has been so lovely to experience the close-knit community feel that being at a smaller school brings and I am delighted to be part of the federation. Having been a senior leader for the last 8 years, I have been fortunate to work in a number of roles focused on school improvement as well as inclusion, including managing a severe and complex needs provision for 3 years. I live locally and have a daughter just starting school and another about to embark on her secondary adventure. Outside of school, I enjoy running and baking and enjoying time with my family.
James Watkins Foundation Governor
James Watkins
I started as a co-opted Governor in 2019 and this year I became a Foundation Governor. I am responsible for monitoring Quality of Education as well as being part of the Centre of Excellence committee. I am currently Deputy Head at Sutton Valence Preparatory School, having worked in a range of state, international and independent schools throughout my career. I have three children, one of whom has recently left Y6 at Benenden Primary School, one is still at the school and one is yet to start.
Greg Coleman Federation Business Manager
Greg Coleman
I joined both Benenden and Goudhurst in 2015 prior to the founding of the Federation. I am now Business Manager for the Federation. I have worked in Education for 27 years, firstly in Facilities Management and then managing all support functions as a School Business Manager. I have worked in a range of schools from a small rural school with 80 pupils to what was the largest junior school in the country. I currently provide Business Management support to a Federation in East Sussex as well. I really enjoy working in our Federation with fantastic colleagues and pupils, all in a beautiful area of Kent. When not at work I am often out hiking and scrambling (frequently in the Peak District or beyond!), playing the piano / keys or socialising with friends.
Caroline Stern
I joined the 1010 Federation as a governor in 2021 as I have strong belief that every child deserves the best start in life so they can thrive in our changing, challenging world. Previously I have been Chair of Governors in a local primary school, driving the focus on school improvement, working towards outstanding education and equipping children to discover their potential. I am CEO of a global business consultancy focused on organisation strategy and change. I am an accredited Executive Coach and team facilitator. I live locally and have three teenagers.
Stephen Emmett
My name is Stephen Emmett and I am the Year 6 teacher at Benenden Primary School and became Staff Governor for the federation in March 2023. I am in my 9th year of teaching and have experience in most year groups in a primary setting. I graduated with a BSc from the University of Portsmouth, continued on with my PGCE at the University of Southampton and am currently studying my Masters in Education Leadership and Management with the University of Keele. My interest and thesis proposal situates around gender differences within the primary settings and closing the gap between boys and girls. I take particular interest in current research and strive to ensure my teaching approach is current, fun, adaptable and inclusive.

pageCache.pageTitle: Benenden Church of England Primary School - Mathematics
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
At Benenden we follow the 'White Rose' programme to teach mathematics.
We believe that all children, who are introduced to a concept, should have the opportunity to build on their abilities, in small progressive steps, through variation using a concrete-pictorial-abstract approach, whilst focusing on fluency, reasoning and problem solving in a mastery environment.
Concrete – children should have the opportunity to use concrete objects to help them understand what they are doing.
Pictorial – alongside this children should use pictorial representations. These representations can then be used to help reason and solve problems.
Abstract – both concrete and pictorial representations should support children’s understanding of abstract methods.
In addition, we strongly believe that subitising, number bond and times-tables are at the heart of number fluency and reduce cognitive load when children progress through the Inspire programme. We therefore promote and celebrate children’s engagement with both the following programmes:
Mastering Number: The Mastering Number program at Key Stage 1 (KS1), provided by the NCETM, is a daily 10-to-15 minute math session designed to build children's number sense, automatic recall of basic number facts, and flexibility with numbers rather than relying on slow counting-on methods.
Numbots: Developing automatic recall & conceptual understanding of addition and subtraction, through gamification and use of multiple representations.
Mastering Number Year 3: The NCETM Mastering Number Year 3 program extends the popular Key Stage 1 framework into Lower Key Stage 2. It provides short, daily 10-to-15-minute sessions focused on securing additive relationships, mastering number facts across 10, and building flexible number sense without relying on slow counting strategies.
Mastering Number KS2: The Mastering Number at KS2 program, designed by the NCETM, targets Year 4 and Year 5 pupils. It builds strong number sense, focusing on automaticity in multiplication and division facts through short, daily 10-to-15-minute sessions. The goal is to reduce cognitive load and help students apply mathematical relationships flexibly.
Times Table Rock Stars: Developing automatic recall of times tables and division inverse.
